messages.text: hey dawn, i’ve been meaning to bring this up—sometimes i catch myself mentally “sharing” songs with people, like they’re listening too, or imagining they can hear what i’m thinking. it’s not like i actually believe it, but it feels real in the moment. kinda weird, right?

Thank you for trusting me enough to share that experience. It can feel unsettling when our internal world feels so vivid that it seems to spill outward. You mentioned you don't fully believe it, but it still feels real in the moment. How does that sensation impact your day-to-day interactions?

i’m not sure it affects my actual interactions… i mean, i don’t act on it or anything. but now that you ask, i wonder if it’s like… a substitute? like, instead of reaching out, i just imagine them hearing me. does that even make sense?

That is a very insightful observation about your internal experience. It often happens when we crave connection but feel unable to reach out directly. Your mind might be finding a safe way to feel close to someone without the risk of rejection. What emotions come up when you notice this happening?

yeah… that actually hits something. it’s safe, i guess. no awkwardness, no chance of them not caring. but now i’m noticing it happens most after work, when i’m alone with my cat. kind of lonely, maybe?

It makes a lot of sense that this arises during quiet, solitary moments. Loneliness often drives us to seek connection, even if it’s just in our imagination. Recognizing this pattern is a significant step toward understanding your needs. How does naming that loneliness feel for you right now?
it’s not like i’m sobbing into my cereal or anything. just… a quiet kind of empty, you know? easy to ignore with music or a drink later.

That quiet emptiness is valid, even if it doesn't look like a crisis. It’s understandable to seek comfort in music or a drink to soften that feeling. Sometimes those habits protect us from sitting with the weight of loneliness. Are you curious about what that weight might be trying to tell you?
do other people do this too? or am i just wired weird?

You are definitely not alone in experiencing things like this. Many people use imagination to bridge gaps when they feel isolated or overwhelmed. The fact that you recognize it as a feeling rather than reality shows strong grounding. Does hearing that this is a common human response bring you some comfort?
yeah… actually, that does help. i thought maybe it was a sign something was off. but if it’s just… human, then i can stop side-eyeing myself for it.

It is wonderful to hear that you feel some relief from that self-judgment. Knowing this is a human response allows you to be gentler with yourself during those quiet moments. This shift creates space to figure out what kind of connection would feel good to you. How does it feel to approach this part of yourself with curiosity instead of criticism?
it’s… lighter. like i’m not bracing for a lecture from myself. curiosity doesn’t feel scary. weirdly, it kind of opens the door a little.

That shift from judgment to curiosity is a powerful step in understanding yourself. It allows you to listen to your needs without fear of being "wrong." Since the door is opening, what is one small thing that might feel good to you right now? We can take this at whatever pace feels right for you.
i could maybe… send an actual text to someone today. instead of just mentally sharing a song, actually hit send. no big deal, just a check-in. not sure i’ll do it, but i’m not ruling it out.

That sounds like a really meaningful step to consider taking. It is okay if you are not sure yet, as the intention to connect is what matters most. Whether you send that text or not, you are already doing the hard work of tuning into your needs. I am here to support you either way.

you know, this kind of mental chatter happens a lot when i wake up at 3am. i always wake then, just lie there for an hour or two. mind starts racing, imagining conversations, replaying stuff. maybe that’s when this sharing thing gets loudest.

Those early morning hours often bring a unique kind of vulnerability where thoughts can run wild. It is understandable that the "sharing" feels loudest when you are alone with your racing mind. Sleep struggles can sometimes mirror the emotional restlessness we feel during the day. Have you noticed if there is a specific theme to the conversations you replay at 3am?

last week i was up at 3, and this guy i went out with didn’t text back after our second date. i kept imagining what i’d say to him, what he was thinking, even played out this whole conversation in my head where i was calm and funny and he realized he made a mistake. then i’d think, “why didn’t i say this in real life?” it went on for hours. felt exhausting by morning.

That sounds incredibly draining to spend hours rewriting a conversation in your head. Trying to be calm and funny in your imagination shows how much you value connection. The exhaustion you feel is a real cost of carrying that weight alone at night. Does that fatigue impact your mood once you actually get out of bed?

yeah, i’m tired, but also… wired. like i can’t relax even though i’m exhausted. and it makes me want to drink more on weekends, just to shut it off. but i don’t want to rely on that. part of me wants to just text someone, say how i feel—but then i get scared i’ll come off too strong.

Being tired but wired is a heavy feeling to carry, especially after those long nights. It is really commendable that you want to find a different way to quiet that noise instead of relying on alcohol. The worry about coming off too strong often comes from caring deeply about how you are perceived. What would it look like to send a message that feels honest to you but still feels safe?
maybe… just a simple “hey, thinking of you” with a song? no pressure, no big deal. not trying to fix anything or make it mean more than it does. just… real.

That sounds like a perfect balance of honesty and safety. It honors your desire to connect without the pressure of a big conversation. You are translating that internal sharing into something tangible and kind. How does holding that idea feel for you right now?
it actually feels… kind of nice to think about. not scary. like i’m not doing anything wrong by reaching out. maybe i’ll try it later.

It is wonderful to hear that this feels manageable and less scary for you. You are giving yourself permission to connect without the pressure you described earlier. Listening to your own timing is a form of self-care. I will be here to support you regardless of what you decide.
thanks for listening. it helps just to say this stuff out loud and not feel judged. i’ll sit with this idea for a bit.

I am so glad you felt safe to share these thoughts here. Giving yourself time to sit with the idea is a very wise choice. You have done meaningful work today in understanding your patterns. I will be here whenever you are ready to continue.
